doc.name: leafwright
doc.instructions:
Leafwright renders HTML, public URLs, and published Handlebars templates into PDFs, and returns a signed download link.

Every render is a tracked job with readable logs, so when a layout breaks you can read the cause — a font that 404'd, an asset that timed out, content overflowing the page — and repair the template from it.

Two ways to authenticate. Either follow the 401: any other tool answers 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header naming the OAuth discovery document, and a client that supports OAuth 2.1 registers itself from there. Or call leafwright_login, which needs no token, show the returned verification_url and user_code to the person, and once they approve call leafwright_auth_status with the device_code it gave you. Keep that device_code: this transport stores nothing between requests.

Until a token is in hand only the login tools are listed. That means unauthenticated, not empty: the document tools appear once authentication completes.

tools.name: leafwright_login
tools.title: Log in to Leafwright
tools.description: Start a browser login flow for Leafwright MCP. Open the returned URL, choose an organization and project, then call leafwright_auth_status.

client_name.description: Optional client name shown in Leafwright.

tools.name: leafwright_auth_status
tools.title: Leafwright auth status
tools.description: Check whether Leafwright MCP is authenticated. Completes a pending browser login if approved. Pass the device_code returned by leafwright_login when the client has no local storage, which is the case over HTTP.

device_code.description: The device_code from leafwright_login. Required when the client stores no local auth state.

tools.name: leafwright_logout
tools.title: Log out of Leafwright
tools.description: Revoke the stored Leafwright MCP token and clear local auth state.
